lens: Fact and integrity audit of /home/user/livewell-land/client/public/essays/is-it-wrong-to-love-your-country.json (updated 2026-10-28) against its claims ledger /home/user/livewell-land/docs/work/essays/ledgers/is-it-wrong-to-love-your-country.md, the BSB chapter files in /home/user/livewell-land/client/public/bible/ch/, the saved ESV copy in the session scratchpad (src/esv-mdbible, lguenth/mdbible), Project Gutenberg texts re-fetched this run from the GITenberg GitHub mirrors (PG #12245 The Defendant, PG #130 Orthodoxy, PG #202 My Bondage and My Freedom), and the integrity rules in /home/user/Livewell-/docs/work/essays/BRIEF.md. Read-only. The published body is identical to the body of docs/work/essays/is-it-wrong-to-love-your-country.md. Every sentence was walked; every checkable claim (about 120: 28 Scripture strings, 22 non-Scripture quotations, the Gallup figures, dates, names, titles and attributions) has a ledger line, and no ledger line is left unverified, open or resting on memory. All 28 Scripture strings matched the saved ESV copy by script, punctuation included (inner quotation marks, LORD/Lord and apostrophes normalized), and each reference matched the verse's sense in the BSB. Every Chesterton quotation and every Douglass quotation drawn from the 1855 extract matched word for word in the Gutenberg texts re-fetched this run. This run used 16 of its 30 web searches on 2026-10-28 and saw search-engine summaries only; a WebFetch of teachingamericanhistory.org failed because the host is outside this session's allowed network domains (it would have to be allowed in the session's network settings to read the 1852 oration directly). No ledger restoration is available: the three corrections were accuracy fixes, the Gallup generational figures are confirmed again as pooled 2021 to 2025, and the one cut for lack of checking (Orthodoxy, 1908) is already restored. One finding: a repeated Scripture fragment is printed without its reference.

findings.where: Two Ways to Get It Wrong, second paragraph: 'It looks down on neighbors who still love the place, quick to say that they have sinned and slow to say, with Nehemiah, "I and my father's house have sinned."'
findings.problem: This is a verbatim ESV quotation (Nehemiah 1:6, from 'Even I and my father's house have sinned', matched by script this run) printed without a reference beside it. The brief requires Scripture to carry its reference wherever it is quoted. The earlier full quotation in the Nehemiah section has '(1:6)', but this one sits three sections later with no reference nearby.
findings.fix: Replace with: slow to say, with Nehemiah, "I and my father's house have sinned" (Nehemiah 1:6).

clean_checks: Gallup, June 2026: 33 percent 'extremely proud', the lowest since the trend began in 2001; Republicans 70, Democrats 14 (independents 28). Search this run cited Gallup's own topline PDF '2026_06_29 Proud to be American Topline and Tabs' plus PJ Media (June 29, 2026), Washington Examiner and KIRO (July 1, 2026): 'the lowest in the trend's 25-year history'. Matches the essay and ledger.

Gallup generational figures: search this run summarized Gallup's own page (news.gallup.com/poll/692150): averages for 2021 to 2025, Gen Z 41, millennials 58, Gen X 71, baby boomers 75, Silent 83, 'extremely' or 'very' proud. The essay's 'In its polls from 2021 through 2025' is correct; correction 1 stands and the writer's 'A year earlier' should not be restored.

Gallup 2024 to 2025 'extremely or very proud': Republicans 85 to 92, Democrats 62 to 36. Confirmed this run (RealClearPolling, Yahoo, Fox News, McClatchy). The White House change between the June 2024 and June 2025 readings is correct.

All 28 Scripture strings (Exodus 20:12; Acts 17:26, 17:27; Genesis 11:4; 1 Samuel 8:5, 8:7; Nehemiah 1:3, 1:4 twice, 1:6 twice, 2:2, 2:3, 2:5; Psalm 137:1, 137:3, 137:4 to 5, 137:9; Ruth 1:15, 1:16 twice; Acts 16:12, 16:21, 22:28; Philippians 3:20; Revelation 21:23, 21:24, 21:26 twice, 21:27; Matthew 10:37) matched the saved ESV text by script, punctuation included. Every reference matches the verse's sense in the BSB chapter files. The three exclamation points are all inside verbatim Scripture (Nehemiah 2:3, Psalm 137:5, Psalm 137:9) and each carries a full reference. No em-dashes.

Unquoted Scripture claims checked against BSB: Hanani from Judah (Neh 1:2), cupbearer (1:11), Chislev to Nisan (1:1, 2:1), 'not sick' (2:2), Deuteronomy 23:3 bars Moabites, Ruth great-grandmother of David (Ruth 4:17), Ruth in Matthew 1:5, Paul's citizenship at Philippi (Acts 16:37), Nehemiah's twelve-year governorship and return to the king (5:14, 13:6), Areopagus and philosophers (Acts 17:18, 22).

Chesterton, The Defendant: re-fetched PG #12245 this run. 'My country, right or wrong ... drunk or sober.', 'would share her troubles to the last', 'the first of all the marks of love is seriousness', 'will always esteem the most candid counsellor the best' all match word for word; the October 1901 prefatory note is present; the contents list ends with 'A DEFENCE OF PATRIOTISM'.

Chesterton, Orthodoxy: re-fetched PG #130 this run. 'a desperate thing--say Pimlico', the Pimlico sentence (THEIRS in capitals) and 'Men did not love Rome because she was great. She was great because they had loved her.' match. The 1908 year was confirmed by the ledger's closing pass and is correctly restored.

Douglass, 1855 extract (PG #202, re-fetched this run): 'This Fourth of July is _yours_, not mine. You may rejoice, I must mourn.', 'How can we sing the Lord's song in a strange land?', 'What to the American slave is your Fourth of July? I answer, a day that reveals to him, more than all other days in the year, the gross injustice and cruelty to which he is the constant victim.', 'your prayers and hymns ... religious parade and solemnity,' and 'mere bombast, fraud, deception, impiety, and hypocrisy', 'false to the past, false to the present' all match. Note, no change needed: these follow Douglass's own 1855 reprint, which the ledger documents, while the 1852 pamphlet's punctuation differs slightly ('What, to the American slave, is your 4th of July?'); both are Douglass's words.

Douglass, 1852-only lines: 'The signers of the Declaration of Independence were brave men.' (search this run: ushistory.org, sentence matches and opens his praise of the founders); 'GLORIOUS LIBERTY DOCUMENT' and 'I do not despair of this country' (search this run: National Constitution Center, battlefields.org; the second opens the conclusion). July 5, 1852, Corinthian Hall, Rochester Ladies' Anti-Slavery Society confirmed by search (Wikipedia, NPS; the NPS invitation reads 'On Monday, July 5th'). July 4, 1852 was a Sunday (computed this run), so correction 3 ('at the holiday') stands.

Lewis, The Four Loves: 'begins to be a demon the moment he begins to be a god' as Lewis's restatement of Rougemont's 'love ceases to be a demon only when he ceases to be a god', in the Introduction (search this run: Wikipedia, lewisiana.nl, booksataglance). Paraphrases of love of home, 'not in the least aggressive. It asks only to be let alone', the beer-and-tea and local-dialect passage, and the 'pennyworth of imagination' line about foreigners confirmed by search (Independent Institute, FEE, C.S. Lewis Institute, Restless Pilgrim). No quotation marks on the paraphrases.

Weil: 'To be rooted is perhaps the most important and least recognized need of the human soul' confirmed by search (technologyandsociety.org, The Conversation, Kingsnorth; 'recognised/recognized' varies by edition). Written in London for the Free French, published later (1949); compassion for one's country set against Hitler's cult of greatness (Christian Century, 'Practicing compassionate patriotism'). Paraphrase, no quotation marks.

Aquinas: ST II-II q.101 a.1, 'man is debtor chiefly to his parents and his country, after God', parents and country as principles of being and government that gave us birth and nourishment, the virtue is piety (search this run: CCEL, clerus.org, isidore.co, aquinas.cc Latin 'post Deum, maxime est homo debitor parentibus et patriae'). Paraphrase is accurate.

Barth and the 1914 manifesto: dated October 4, 1914 (German History in Documents); Barth found 'almost all of my theological teachers' among the signers and could no longer follow 'their ethics and dogmatics or their understanding of the Bible and of history'; Harnack signed (search this run: Wikipedia 'Karl Barth', printculture.com). The essay's paraphrase has no quotation marks.

Barmen: synod May 29 to 31, 1934; drafted by Barth with Hans Asmussen; first thesis 'the one Word of God whom we have to hear, and whom we have to trust and obey' (search this run: gci.org, EKD). German Christians' programmatic papers 1932 to 1933, so 'By 1933' is safe.

Resident Aliens (1989, Abingdon), Hauerwas and Willimon: church as colony, rejection of America or any country as a Christian nation (search this run: Wikipedia summary, Christian Century 25th-anniversary forum). Fair to both living authors; the war sentence is attributed to the pacifist tradition, not quoted from the book.

Bonhoeffer: 'I must live through this difficult period of our national history with the Christian people of Germany' confirmed by search (Samuel Marks Substack, 3quarksdaily, New Republic). June 1939 arrival and a July departure supported (Fortress Press: returned just before September 1939; a genealogy index lists New York arrival June 12 and Southampton arrival July 13, 1939). One search summary wrongly said he returned in 1940; the main sources and the ledger agree on July 1939. Arrest 1943, hanging at Flossenburg April 9, 1945, a month before V-E Day, consistent with the ledger.

Living persons: only Hauerwas and Willimon are named; the sentence about them is supported. The left/right and generational characterizations are about groups, marked as interpretation in the ledger, and applied with the same instrument to both sides.

Links: /writing/what-christian-nationalism-is-and-is-not, /writing/when-patriotism-becomes-a-gospel and /writing/was-america-founded-as-a-christian-nation are all present in docs/work/essays/link-targets.json (checked by script this run).
Biography: 'I'm raising five sons in this country' is within the confirmed facts; no title, years, book count or scene is claimed.

Restorations (g): none proposed. Corrections 2 and 3 were accuracy fixes; correction 1 is confirmed again by Gallup's own page as pooled 2021 to 2025; Orthodoxy's 1908 is already restored. The writer's own cuts (Tolstoy, Mouw, Isaiah 60:3, Weil's 'beautiful, precious, fragile and perishable', Bonhoeffer's ship and arrival date, Douglass's 1847 line) were the writer's choices, not verification cuts, and none is needed.
